title: Chat inference contractual SLOs, acceptance criteria and progressive rollout gates
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: PRD-level ticket to define deterministic SLO targets, error budgets, acceptance criteria, and progressive rollout/rollback gates for the Chat (streaming + non-streaming) inference endpoint for hosted customers. This ticket codifies measurable contractual commitments across workload classes (interactive short prompts, multi-turn chat, long completions) and defines automation for canary promotions, automatic rollbacks, and controlled degradations under capacity or quality regressions. Scope includes: SLO targets, measurement methods, alerting thresholds, acceptance tests for new runtime changes, and rollout gating automation. Out of scope: billing/pricing adjustments and on-prem private deployment changes (separate PM ticket).
proposed_slos: Tiering: Free (trial), Standard, Enterprise — each has distinct latency/availability bands
Interactive short prompts (<=256 tokens): p50 <= 30ms, p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 300ms for Enterprise; Standard: p50 <= 40ms, p95 <= 180ms, p99 <= 450ms; Free: best-effort (no contractual SLA)
Multi-turn chat (session length typical 256-1024 tokens): steady-state p50 <= 45ms, p95 <= 200ms, p99 <= 600ms for Enterprise; cold-start extra 20-40ms penalty included in SLO window
Long completions (>1024 tokens): throughput-target SLO — median token throughput >= X tokens/s per GPU (measured by runtime telemetry) and tail latency for first token p95 <= 800ms
Availability: Enterprise 99.95% monthly uptime (error budget 0.05% ~ 21.6 minutes/month); Standard 99.9%; Free no SLA
API error rate budget: Maximum 0.5% 5xx errors per month for Enterprise; alert at 0.2% sustained over 15m; throttle/429s excluded from 5xx budget but counted for user-impact monitoring

Quality regressions: Model output correctness SLOs measured via regression sets — no more than 3% degradation in top-line eval score vs baseline per release; automated reject if >5% degradation detected in canary
Maintenance windows: permissible scheduled maintenance up to 120 minutes/month excluded from uptime calculation if announced >=72h and not impacting contracted regions
acceptance_criteria: Defined and documented measurement spec: exact telemetry signals, aggregation windows, and query examples for each SLO (p50/p95/p99 calculations).
Dashboards: Per-tier live dashboards in Console showing SLOs, rolling 7/30 day windows, and historical error budgets with drilldowns to route/model-level metrics.
Automated checks: CI acceptance test that fails PRs changing runtime scheduling if canary telemetry shows SLO breach for >15 minutes during test harness runs (synthetic load).
Alerting: Paging and on-call runbook created for SLO burn >25% of monthly error budget in 24h, and automatic escalation when >50% burned in 24h.

Rollout gating: Canary promotion automation configured with metric gates (p95 latency, 5xx rate, model-regression score) and documented thresholds; gates must be validated in staging and preview before production canary.
Contract text: Updated SLA clause drafted for Legal with clear definitions (measurement window, exclusions, credits formula) and sign-off from Legal and Finance.
Load-tested validation: End-to-end traffic replay demonstrating SLO attainment for Standard and Enterprise under representative workload mixes (chat-heavy, completion-heavy).

Acceptance tests for fallback behavior: When primary runtime exceeds latency band, configured fallback to lower-capacity model variant must occur within 120s and preserve correctness above defined baseline.
rollout_gates: Phase 0 - Lab/staging: synthetic scenarios + regression harness (no customer traffic). Metrics: baseline p95, 5xx=0, eval regression <=1%
Phase 1 - Shadow canary (1% of prod traffic): monitor for 30m minimum and gate on p95 latency delta <= +10% and 5xx delta <= +0.1%; automated rollback if gate fails.

Phase 2 - Incremental canary: 5% for 1h -> 25% for 2h -> 100% if stable. Promotion requires p95 latency within thresholds and model-eval pass. Failure at any stage triggers automatic demote to previous stable tier and a P1 incident runbook.
Automatic rollback triggers: sustained p95 latency increase >20% for 15m, 5xx increase >0.5% absolute for 10m, or eval regression >5% in canary windows.

Controlled degradation path: If capacity constrained, route new requests to cached responses (if meeting correctness check) for up to 10% of traffic and return structured ‘degraded: true’ in response; must be instrumented and visible in Console.
Manual gates: Legal/CS must approve enterprise-impacting contract language changes before final SLA publication.
notes: Measurement approach decision: use server-side egress timing + token emission metric instead of client round-trip to avoid client network noise; record both for troubleshooting but only server-side used for contractual measurements.
Batching impact: SLO calculation will normalize for batching delays by attributing per-request kernel start time; Eng to provide instrumentation RFC (ENG-4311) before implementation.
Cache semantics: Prefix/KV cache hits counted separately; SLOs apply to origin model to avoid masking effects of high cache hit rates.
Tradeoffs: Tighter p99 targets add cost — proposed bands align Enterprise to higher-cost low-latency config (reserved capacity).
